verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Same two inequalities, with the C^k_η norm written out and ω_fin split into its two constituent widths. (i) Norm: the paper fixes on p.150 that "Bounds in C^k_η refer only to parameter derivatives, uniformly for −1 ≤ η ≤ 1"; the Lean writes that literally as ∀ n ≤ N, ∀ η ∈ J, |iteratedDeriv n · η| ≤ ·, with ClosedIntervalJetAlgebra.J = Icc (-1) 1. One constant B (resp. Cjoin) serves all orders n ≤ N instead of the paper's per-k 𝓑_k, C_k^join; passing between the two is taking a finite maximum over k ≤ N (exists_linear_Ck_constants does exactly this with finite_majorant for Cnat). (ii) Objects: ℓ_i ↔ StockReference.endpointLog T κ w₁ w₂ q.C, which endpointLog_eq_physical shows is log(C·√220·F(110,·)) = log(C E(X_i,·)) since the paper has E = √(2X)·ϕ/C (p.149 (4.4)) and X_i = 110 (p.150); G_i ↔ endpointU, which endpointU_eq_physical shows is U(110,·); U_* ↔ NaturalAxisData.U j = 4η+j, the paper's U_* = 4η+j₀ of (B.1); the reference's radius0 is 4/Λ = X_0 (reference_radius). (iii) Parameters: t_1 ↔ T, κ_0 ↔ κ, and ω_fin ↔ w₁+w₂ — the paper defines ω_fin as the sum of the logarithmic radial lengths of the final axial cutoff and of the interpolation of a to .8, and in the Lean w₁ is the width of `step b w₁` in axialSlope (the axial cutoff) and w₂ the width of `step (b+w₁) w₂` in angularSlope (the ramp to the constant slope −2/5 = −.4). (iv) Quantifier order, which is the content of the prose under (B.32): Cnat is ∃-bound before ∀Λ and before ∀q : Choice d Λ, so it is independent of Λ and of the amplitude C (Choice carries C with 1 ≤ C); B and Cjoin are ∃-bound after Λ but before q and before T, w₁, w₂, so they may depend on Λ but not on C nor on smaller transition widths. (v) Hypothesis side, where the Lean is the more general of the two: κ ∈ Icc 0 1 rather than the paper's κ_0 ∈ (0,1/2), and T > 0 with no upper bound t_1 ≤ t̄; the Lean adds 1 ≤ Λ and AxisReference.stabilityScale … ≤ Λ, which is the paper's standing "after increasing Λ" of §B.5.
